title: Danish Supermarket Tests Humanoid Robot Workers
paragraphs: Humanoid robots are being tested in a supermarket in Denmark, where they are learning to put products on shelves.

The trial is being carried out by Salling Group, Denmark's largest retailer, which runs more than 2,000 stores in six European countries. The robots are being tested at a Føtex supermarket near the capital, Copenhagen. They were developed by Hive Robots, a Danish start-up company, and built by the Chinese robot maker Unitree.

The robots have been training since June 2026. At the moment, human operators guide every one of their movements, which helps the robots' artificial intelligence learn how to handle different products. The robots practice picking up products and placing them on shelves again and again.

The aim of the project is to reduce the workload of supermarket staff. According to Føtex, workers spend between 40% and 50% of their time refilling shelves. The retailer hopes that the robots can take over some of this repetitive work, so that employees can spend more time helping customers. According to Hive Robots, it is also difficult to find young workers to do this job.

The goal is for the robots to be able to restock shelves on their own by early 2027. They will mainly work at night, when the supermarket is closed. In the future, the robots might also check expiry dates, find empty shelves and spot products that have been put in the wrong place.

However, the robots still have a long way to go. They are currently slower than human workers, and they need close supervision. In addition, Danish law would have to change before robots could work on their own among shoppers. For now, the robots will focus on working at night, away from customers.
It is also not yet clear whether the robots will save as much labor as the retailer hopes.
